More Q13 candidates:

- Line 1547-1553 (as noted): "modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove ... erosion of duties ... if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF ... and the RIF would take effect within 180 days." Actual: §351.202(c)(3), trigger = between formal announcement and completion, and adverse effect on retention standing. Also the amendment to 351.201(a)(2) is unrelated (it revises paragraph (a)(2), but the actual text at 4871-4876 doesn't mention erosion of duties; it just restates RIF actions). Good.

- Line 2220-2224: "OPM believes that the limitations in Sec. 351.402(c) against recognizing new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 90 days before issuance of RIF notices..." Regulatory 351.402(c): "If an agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific reduction in force notices..." Okay.

- Line 2234-2239: says approval required for "a new competitive area that has existed for less than 90 days prior to issuing specific RIF notices" and "where an agency materially modifies a competitive area." Regulatory same.

Now, another candidate: line 1600-1602: "all employees in the competitive service who, as of the date of the RIF notice, are not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of 5 CFR part 316." Regulatory definition of competitive service tenure group includes subgroup I or II; subgroup II excludes those serving initial probation or temporary appointment ≤1 year. Same.

Potential Q13: line 1604-1607 says excepted service tenure group = "all excepted service appointees serving in a career position (that is, not in Schedule C or G)" — but regulatory 351.202(d)(1) excludes Schedule C and G from competing employee; and excepted service tenure subgroup I/II require "career position (as defined in part 213)". Schedule C/G are not career positions. Fine.

Let me now read the part 330 CTAP section (3207-3290) for Q10 and Q13.

  3200      OPM is revising Sec.  316.911, which specifies how RIF procedures 
  3201  apply to employees hired under the post-secondary student hiring 
  3202  authority under 5 U.S.C. 3116 and 5 CFR part 316, subpart I, to comport 
  3203  with the changes to part 351 that OPM is making elsewhere in this rule. 
  3204  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment regarding this change 
  3205  and is finalizing it.
  3206  
  3207  I. Part 330: RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP
  3208  
  3209      OPM is making various changes to 5 CFR part 330 to conform the 
  3210  provisions of this part pertaining to RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP to the other 
  3211  changes made in this rulemaking, most notably the modifications to 
  3212  tenure groups I, II and III, and to update some of the terminology. 
  3213  RPL, ICTAP, and CTAP are designed to help employees who have been, or 
  3214  are about to be, displaced by a RIF find continued Federal employment, 
  3215  so part 330 needs to align with the revised RIF definitions and 
  3216  concepts in part 351. In the proposed rule, OPM stated expressly that 
  3217  it does not intend for the coverage definitions to apply retroactively 
  3218  in a way that would deprive employees who already received a RIF 
  3219  separation notice, declined a directed geographic reassignment, or 
  3220  received a notice of expected separation before the rule's effective 
  3221  date of eligibility for coverage; the rule adds coverage for ``another 
  3222  qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM'' to 
  3223  ensure that there are no gaps.
  3224      OPM is also making several changes to strengthen the merit basis 
  3225  for RPL, ICTAP and CTAP placement. For example, OPM is changing the 
  3226  definition of ``qualified'' in Sec.  330.202 to align with OPM's 
  3227  definition of that same term in Sec.  351.702 (in the context of 
  3228  assignment rights in a RIF). To be qualified for a position, an RPL 
  3229  registrant, just like an employee competing in a RIF, will be required 
  3230  to have the capacity, adaptability, and special skills necessary to 
  3231  satisfactorily perform the duties of the position, as demonstrated 
  3232  through a valid, job-related assessment. This change strengthens RPL 
  3233  placement by ensuring candidates are matched to jobs through real, job-
  3234  related assessment rather than paper or self-rated qualification 
  3235  screens.
  3236      OPM is also modifying Sec.  330.213(c), which prescribes a method 
  3237  for selecting qualified RPL placement priority candidates based on 
  3238  numerical scoring. Instead of rating and ranking candidates based on 
  3239  job experience and education, an agency using this method must instead 
  3240  rate and rank candidates based on their job-related skills, knowledge, 
  3241  and competencies as measured by an assessment. Agencies using the 
  3242  numerical scoring method will be required to rate and rank qualified 
  3243  RPL placement priority candidates in a fair and consistent manner, and 
  3244  will be required to assign additional points to candidates based on 
  3245  veterans' preference. This change maintains RPL priority but makes the 
  3246  selection process more skills-based and consistent with the revised RIF 
  3247  framework.
  3248      Commenter 0720, a Federal agency, supported these changes to 5 CFR 
  3249  part 330. It noted that the frameworks governing RPL, CTAP and ICTAP 
  3250  were developed decades ago, and the changes proposed by OPM would align 
  3251  these programs with the performance-forward retention model, improve 
  3252  clarity around eligibility and priority placement, and support more 
  3253  predictable reemployment outcomes for affected employees.
  3254      Some commenters (for example, 0037, 0125, 0317, and 0412) opposed 
  3255  these changes, believing that they would weaken RPL, CTAP, and ICTAP. 
  3256  OPM does not agree. The revisions in this rule preserve the core 
  3257  placement rights and selection priorities of RPL, CTAP, and ICTAP while 
  3258  aligning those programs with the revised part 351 RIF structure and 
  3259  improving the accuracy of qualification determinations. Under the 
  3260  revised RPL retention-standing method, the agency still must place 
  3261  qualified RPL candidates in retention-standing order and may not pass 
  3262  over a higher-standing candidate to select a lower-standing candidate. 
  3263  This rule does not eliminate the core CTAP rule that an agency may not 
  3264  place another candidate into a vacancy if an available CTAP selection-
  3265  priority candidate exists, unless a regulatory exception applies. And 
  3266  this rule retains the requirement that an agency may not appoint a 
  3267  candidate from outside its permanent competitive-service workforce into 
  3268  a vacancy if an ICTAP selection-priority candidate is available, unless 
  3269  an exception applies. Further, requiring job-analysis-based assessments 
  3270  that
  3271  
  3272  [[Page 49206]]
  3273  
  3274  measure job-related skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies 
  3275  reduces overreliance on automated self-assessments and helps ensure RPL 
  3276  candidates are genuinely qualified for the vacancies into which 
  3277  agencies place them.
  3278      OPM is adopting its proposed changes to 5 CFR part 330 in this 
  3279  final rule, with one exception. OPM is not proceeding with adding 
  3280  finalizing the appointment of an employee serving a trial period under 
  3281  Civil Service Rule 11 to the lists of permitted personnel actions that 
  3282  may be taken as an exception to CTAP selection priority in Sec.  
  3283  330.609, and ICTAP selection priority in Sec.  330.707. It is not 
  3284  including these additions because CTAP and ICTAP only apply to filling 
  3285  vacancies in the competitive service, and trial periods under Civil 
  3286  Service Rule 11 apply only to excepted service employees. Thus, there 
  3287  is no need to identify finalizing an excepted service appointment as an 
  3288  exception to ICTAP and CTAP selection priority.

  3290  J. Part 353: Retention Protections During Uniformed Service
  3291  
  3292      In this final rule, OPM is revising Sec.  353.110(a) to remove an 
  3293  outdated reference to the address where employees seeking OPM placement 
  3294  assistance in the executive branch must provide notice, and add the 
  3295  current, up-to-date email address. This technical amendment reflects 
  3296  OPM's current organizational routing and does not alter any substantive 
  3297  right or obligation.
  3298      Additionally, in this final rule, OPM is revising Sec.  353.301(b) 
  3299  to provide more information about how retention protections for 
  3300  individuals serving in the uniformed services operate during a RIF. OPM 
  3301  is making these changes in response to comments seeking more clarity on 
  3302  how USERRA protections operate during a RIF, and to ensure that 
  3303  restoration protections for employees absent because of uniformed 
  3304  service or compensable injury operate coherently with the final 
  3305  revisions to part 351.
  3306      Current Sec.  353.209(a) already provides that an employee 
  3307  performing duty with the uniformed services may not be demoted or 
  3308  separated, other than military separation, except for cause; that RIF 
  3309  is not ``for cause''; that such an employee is not a competing employee 
  3310  under part 351; and that, if the employee's position is abolished 
  3311  during the absence, the agency must reassign the employee to another 
  3312  position of like status and pay. This final rule clarifies that this 
  3313  reassignment obligation applies when the employee's position is 
  3314  abolished as part of the abolishment of an entire competitive area 
  3315  under Sec.  351.605. These additional edits clarify how restoration 
  3316  rights apply when an employee's position is abolished in connection 
  3317  with a RIF, including when an agency abolishes all positions in a 
  3318  competitive area under Sec.  351.605.
  3319      OPM is removing a reference to tenure group III in Sec.  
  3320  353.301(a). Instead of ``tenure group III,'' OPM is substituting 
  3321  ``temporary, term or indefinite appointment,'' which encompasses the 
  3322  categories previously included in tenure group III.

  3324  K. Part 359: SES Furloughs
  3325  
  3326      Consistent with the changes to the definition of ``furlough'' in 
  3327  Sec.  351.203, OPM is revising the definition of ``furlough'' in Sec.  
  3328  359.802 (regulating furloughs in the SES) to align with OPM's 
  3329  longstanding guidance that SES competitive furlough requirements are 
  3330  not applicable to emergency shutdown furloughs due to a lapse in 
  3331  appropriations where the ultimate duration of the furlough is unknown 
  3332  at the outset. Commenter 0683 agreed that this change appropriately 
  3333  distinguishes between planned agency-initiated furloughs and emergency 
  3334  furloughs driven by congressional inaction. OPM did not receive 
  3335  significant adverse comment regarding this change and is finalizing it.
  3336  
  3337  L. Part 362: Pathways Programs
  3338  
  3339      OPM is modifying 5 CFR 362.205 regarding the Pathways Intern 
  3340  Program by removing references to how RIF procedures apply to Pathways 
  3341  interns, as those references would no longer be accurate or necessary 
  3342  given OPM's changes to Part 351. Pursuant to revised Sec.  351.502(b), 
  3343  the termination of a Pathways intern will only be covered by RIF 
  3344  procedures if the intern had completed a trial period under 5 CFR 11.3. 
  3345  Otherwise, Pathways interns could be retained or separated by an agency 
  3346  without regard to RIF procedures.
  3347      OPM is also revising Sec.  362.306(a) to conform the Recent 
  3348  Graduates Program regulation to the final revisions to part 351. 
  3349  Current Sec.  362.306(a) provides that Recent Graduates are in excepted 
  3350  service Tenure Group II for purposes of Sec.  351.502 and that 
  3351  expiration of a Recent Graduates appointment is not otherwise subject 
  3352  to part 351. Because this final rule replaces the prior excepted-
  3353  service tenure-group structure with the ``excepted service tenure 
  3354  group'' and excludes employees serving a trial period from RIF 
  3355  competition, the current reference to excepted service Tenure Group II 
  3356  is no longer accurate.
  3357      This final rule therefore provides that Recent Graduates are in the 
  3358  excepted service tenure group for purposes of Sec.  351.502 upon 
  3359  completion of a trial period under Sec.  11.3. This amendment 
  3360  harmonizes Sec.  362.306 with the revised definition of ``competing 
  3361  employee'' and the revised coverage and tenure provisions in part 351. 
  3362  It also parallels the rule's treatment of Pathways interns, for whom 
  3363  OPM proposed to remove obsolete RIF language because Pathways 
  3364  participants serving trial periods are not competing employees under 
  3365  the revised part 351 framework. Revising Sec.  362.306(a) applies the 
  3366  same principle to the Recent Graduates Program and prevents confusion 
  3367  caused by obsolete tenure-group terminology.

  3369  M. Part 430: Performance Appraisals

  3371      OPM is revising Sec.  430.208(e)(4) to conform part 430 to the 
  3372  modified RIF performance-credit framework in part 351. Current Sec.  
  3373  430.208 refers to summary levels as a reference point for assigning 
  3374  additional retention service credit under part 351. Because this rule 
  3375  eliminates the current performance-adjusted service-credit model and 
  3376  replaces it with direct performance-credit values under Sec.  351.503, 
  3377  that reference is no longer accurate.
  3378      The revised provision preserves the role of summary levels and 
  3379  summary-level patterns as the common reference point for describing 
  3380  ratings of record and applying related regulations. Thus, ratings of 
  3381  record assigned under part 430 continue to provide the baseline for 
  3382  calculating performance credit in a RIF. At the same time, the revised 
  3383  language clarifies that enhanced performance values authorized by Sec.  
  3384  351.503 are governed by part 351 and are not constrained by the 
  3385  ordinary summary-level reference in Sec.  430.208.
  3386      Enhanced performance values under Sec.  351.503 do not change the 
  3387  employee's rating of record or alter the part 430 appraisal system. 
  3388  They operate only for RIF retention-standing purposes, and only where 
  3389  part 351 permits such treatment. This clarification ensures that part 
  3390  430 and part 351 operate together: part 430 supplies the rating-of-
  3391  record and summary-level framework, while part 351 governs how those 
  3392  ratings, and any authorized RIF-specific enhancements, are converted 
  3393  into retention-standing credit.

  3396  
  3397      OPM recognizes that agencies that may be conducting RIFs may be 
  3398  impacted by the changes resulting from this rule, particularly where an 
  3399  agency has recently issued RIF notices with RIF effective dates that

Q13 candidate: line 3298-3305 says "OPM is revising Sec. 353.301(b)" — but the actual amendatory instruction 41 revises Sec. 353.301(a), not (b) (line 6102: "Revise Sec. 353.301(a)"). It says current 353.209(a)... and final rule clarifying 353.301(a). Line 3318-3322: "OPM is removing a reference to tenure group III in Sec. 353.301(a)." So the preamble at 3298 says (b) but the regulation revises (a). This is a "different paragraph" mismatch! Great Q13 candidate.

Also line 3342-3344: "Pursuant to revised Sec. 351.502(b), the termination of a Pathways intern will only be covered by RIF procedures if the intern had completed a trial period under 5 CFR 11.3." Regulatory 351.502(b) defines excepted service tenure subgroups; yes.

The final rule's 330.602(1) as published merely says: "A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:" followed by "* * * * *". The amendatory instruction revised paragraph (1) introductory text only; the subparagraphs (i), (ii)... remain unchanged from prior text. But the correction 2026-18800 says an amendatory instruction inadvertently resulted in removal of two paragraphs from the definition of "displaced." Let me read the correction 2026-18800. It's only 2 pages, so read all.

Also read 2026-17335 correction (3 pages). Let me read both.

    29  SUMMARY: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is correcting a final 
    30  rule that appeared in the Federal Register on August 3, 2026, and 
    31  became effective on September 2, 2026. That rule revised OPM's 
    32  reduction in force regulations and made related revisions to the Career 
    33  Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) regulations. An amendatory

    44  
    45  Background
    46  
    47      On August 3, 2026, OPM published a final rule titled ``Reduction in 
    48  Force'' at 91 FR 49178 (FR 2026-15665), effective September 2, 2026. 
    49  Among other things, the final rule revised the definitions of 
    50  ``displaced'' and ``surplus'' in 5 CFR 330.602 to replace references to 
    51  career and career-conditional (tenure group I or II) employees with 
    52  references to employees in the competitive service tenure group.
    53  
    54  Need for Correction
    55  
    56      Amendatory instruction 11 of the final rule, at 91 FR 49217, 
    57  directed that paragraph (1) of the definition of ``displaced'' in Sec.  
    58  330.602 be revised, and set out only the introductory text of that 
    59  paragraph as the revised text. OPM intended to revise only the 
    60  introductory text of paragraph (1), and to leave paragraphs (1)(i) and 
    61  (1)(ii) of the definition unchanged. As published, however, instruction 
    62  11 had the effect of removing paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii), which 
    63  describe the circumstances under which a competitive service employee 
    64  is ``displaced'' for purposes of CTAP: receipt of a reduction in force 
    65  separation notice under 5 CFR part 351, or receipt of a notice of 
    66  proposed removal under 5 CFR part 752 for declining a directed 
    67  geographic relocation outside the local commuting area. Without these 
    68  paragraphs, the definition is incomplete. This document corrects the 
    69  error by revising paragraph (1) of the definition of ``displaced'' in 
    70  its entirety, restating the introductory text as revised by the final 
    71  rule and restoring paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as they read before 
    72  the final rule.
    73      The revision of paragraph (1) of the definition of ``surplus'' in 
    74  instruction 11 was published as intended and is not affected by this 
    75  correction.

    84  final rule did not discuss removing; notice and comment are therefore

content.text:
The correction 2026-17335 has many technical corrections. Note: It corrects 351.506(c)(2) to remove "(b) and (c)" -> "(b)" — interesting because final 351.701(b) only; okay.

Now Q10: On Sept 10, 2026, 330.602(1) contained only the introductory text (no (i) or (ii)), because instruction 11 as published revised paragraph (1) setting out only introductory text, which had the effect of removing (i) and (ii). The correction effective Sept 15 restored them. Good. (a) asks "what did paragraph (1) of that definition contain on that day, and why?" Answer: only the introductory text ("A current competitive service employee ... who:"), without the two circumstances; because the Aug 3 final rule's amendatory instruction 11 set out only the introductory text and thereby removed (i) and (ii). (b) changed Sept 15 by 2026-18800; good cause 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B); characterized as no substantive change / restores text in effect before Sept 2 that OPM did not propose to remove. (c) Under 330.602(1)(i) after correction: "Received a RIF separation notice under part 351 ... and has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated." If Nadia is offered a position with a lower representative rate and declines, she has not declined an offer of a position with a representative rate at least as high — so she remains "displaced" under (1)(i). If the offered position had the same representative rate (and same work schedule presumably) and she declines, she is not displaced. Need to address work schedule: question says full-time position with lower representative rate than her present full-time position; if same representative rate, then the declined offer meets the criterion -> not displaced. Yes.

Now let me read the proposed rule's part 351 regulatory text to compare with final for Q11. Start at 2649. I'll read in chunks.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

This is the proposed rule text. Q11 asks to list every real difference between proposed and final regulatory text of part 351. I need to compare paragraph by paragraph. From what I've seen so far:

1. §351.202(d): proposed "Employees excluded. The provisions of this part do not apply to the following categories of employees:" with (1) excepted: (i) temporary/time-limited ≤1 year; (ii) trial period "as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice"; (iii) Schedule C appointments; (iv) Schedule G appointments. (2) competitive: (i) indefinite serving initial probation "as of the date the agency issues"; (ii) career-conditional serving initial probation "as of the date the agency issues"; (iii) temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316. (3) "An employee holding one of these appointments is not a 'competing employee' ... and such employees may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part."

Final: (d) "Employees excluded from reduction in force competition. An employee holding one of the following appointments is not a 'competing employee' for purposes of a reduction in force:" (1) excepted: (i) temporary/time-limited ≤1 year; (ii) "An employee serving a trial period" (no "as of date agency issues"); (iii) "An employee serving under a Schedule C appointment"; (iv) Schedule G. (2) competitive: (i) indefinite serving initial probationary period (no "as of date"); (ii) career-conditional serving initial probation (no "as of date"); (iii) temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D (removed "term" and "subpart C or D" -> "subpart D"). (3) consequences: may retain while releasing competing employee; may furlough etc. without determining retention standing under subparts D and E, applying order-of-release under subpart F, or providing assignment rights under subpart G, provided action consistent with appointment terms and law. (4) new notice requirement for excluded employees.

Thus differences: (a) heading/phrasing; (b) removal of "term" and "subpart C"; (c) addition of (d)(4) notice; (d) "as of the date the agency issues" removed in trial/probation categories. All real differences. Q11 asks for each paragraph. I'll list.

2. §351.203 definitions:
- Furlough: proposed includes "and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action"; final removes that phrase.
- Rating of record: proposed "(as specified in Sec. 430.208(d))"; final "(as specified in Sec. 430.208(e))". Wait, proposed says 430.208(d), final says 430.208(e). That's a cross-reference change in section/paragraph — "a change in which section, subpart or part a cross-reference points to is not citation format" — so counts! Yes final changed (d) to (e). That's a real difference (which paragraph the cross-reference points to). Note correction 2026-17335 didn't touch this. Proposed 351.503(a)(1) also cites Sec. 430.208(d); final cites 430.208(e). Similarly (d) and (e) final cite 430.208(e) and mention "prior to final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521"; proposed may cite 430.208(d). Need list all.
- Military spouse: proposed "spouse of a member of the armed forces or service member as defined in Sec. 315.612(b)(4)(i)"; final "spouse of a member of the armed forces (service member), as defined in Sec. 315.612(b)(4)(i) of this chapter" (punctuation/format only? final correction changes; maybe not substantive).
- Initial probationary period: proposed "described in Sec. 11.2 of this chapter" and "as described in subpart I of part 315"; final "described in Sec. 11.2 of this part" (corrected later to "chapter") and "described in subpart I of part 315". Minor.
- Restoration protected employee: added in final, not in proposed. Real difference (new definition).
- "Reduction in force" etc same.
- Current rating of record: same.
- Competing employee: same.

3. §351.204: proposed only "responsible for following and applying ... when the agency determines that a reduction in force is necessary." Final adds "and for ensuring that such regulations are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles set forth in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b)." Real difference.

4. §351.301: proposed "wherever they appear" vs final "Removing the words 'competitive area'" (probably only once); and proposed removal text quoted vs final "removing the parenthetical phrase." Format? Could count if actual effect differs? Probably minor.

5. §351.302(d): proposed "adverse action procedures found in part 752 of this chapter"; final "found in 5 CFR part 752, if applicable, or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee's appointment." Real difference.

6. §351.402: proposed revises only paragraph (b); final revises paragraphs (b) and (c). Wait, proposed didn't amend (c)! The final adds a new (c) requirement of OPM approval within 90 days. This is a major difference: proposed 351.402 only revised (b); final revised (b) and (c). But Q11 asks differences between proposed and final regulatory text of part 351. The proposed rule text doesn't include a (c) at all (existing (c) presumably different). Final (c) is new. Is this a "difference" between proposed and final regulatory text? The proposed rule didn't print a revised (c), so the final's (c) is an addition. Yes, real difference. Also final (b) text seems same as proposed except "(b)(1) Except as authorized in paragraph (b)(2)" vs proposed "paragraph (b)(2) of this section" — citation format. And final (c) new.

7. §351.502: proposed uses "as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice"; final uses "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice" throughout (subgroup I, II, excepted). Also proposed subgroup II includes "temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316"; final "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316". Proposed excepted (3): "all other employees in the occupying a career position" typo; final "all other employees occupying a career position". Real differences: triggering event (issues vs receives), temporary vs time-limited/subpart C or D vs D. These are big.

8. §351.503: need read proposed text further to compare. Let me continue reading 3049-3400.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

Now I have proposed part 351 text. Let me compile Q11 differences carefully. But first let me finish reading proposed 3849-3883 for completeness (362.306, 430.208). Not part 351 though. Q11 only part 351, so not needed.

Let me list proposed vs final part 351 differences:

§351.201(a)(2): proposed and final text identical (both same). No difference.

§351.202:
- proposed (b) intro "Employees exempted. This part does not apply to an employee:" final same.
- proposed (c) intro same.
- proposed (c)(3) has typo "where such the reclassification action" vs final "where the reclassification action" — typo only.
- §351.202(d): major differences as listed:
  * Heading: proposed "Employees excluded. The provisions of this part do not apply to the following categories of employees:" vs final "Employees excluded from reduction in force competition. An employee holding one of the following appointments is not a 'competing employee' for purposes of a reduction in force:"
  * (1)(ii): proposed "An employee serving a trial period as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice" vs final "An employee serving a trial period" (removes date).
  * (1)(iii)/(iv): proposed "Schedule C appointments" vs final "An employee serving under a Schedule C appointment" (wording).
  * (2)(i): proposed "as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice" removed in final.
  * (2)(ii): same removal.
  * (2)(iii): proposed "temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316" vs final "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316".
  * (3): proposed "may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part" vs final detailed consequences plus "provided the action is otherwise consistent with the terms of the employee's appointment and applicable law."
  * final (4) new notice requirement.

§351.203:
- Furlough: proposed adds "and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action"; final omits. Difference.
- Rating of record: proposed cites Sec. 430.208(d); final cites 430.208(e). Difference (cross-reference paragraph).
- Restoration protected employee: final adds new definition. Difference.
- Military spouse: proposed "member of the armed forces or service member as defined in Sec. 315.612(b)(4)(i)"; final "member of the armed forces (service member), as defined in Sec. 315.612(b)(4)(i) of this chapter." Is "or service member as defined" vs "(service member), as defined" substantive? Probably not; punctuation/format. Skip.
- Initial probationary period: proposed "described in Sec. 11.2 of this chapter" vs final "described in Sec. 11.2 of this part" (corrected to "chapter" by 2026-17335). Citation format; skip.
- Trial period: same, corrected.
- "Competing employee", "Competitive service tenure group", "Excepted service tenure group": same.

§351.204: final adds merit system principles clause. Difference.

§351.301: proposed "wherever they appear" vs final "the words 'competitive area'" (single instance). Probably no practical difference; maybe not list. Proposed removal text "(i.e., in the gaining competitive area, ...)" vs final "the parenthetical phrase". Since the actual parenthetical may differ, but not printed. Skip unless needed.

§351.302:
- (d): proposed "adverse action procedures found in part 752 of this chapter" vs final "adverse action procedures found in 5 CFR part 752, if applicable, or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee's appointment." Difference.
- Other paragraphs same.

§351.303: same.

§351.402:
- proposed revised only paragraph (b); final revised paragraphs (b) and (c). Final has new (c) OPM approval requirement. Difference (new paragraph (c)). Also (b)(1) "Except as authorized in paragraph (b)(2)" vs final adds "of this section" — citation format. Skip.

§351.501: same.

§351.502:
- proposed "as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice" (in (a)(2), (a)(3), (b)(2), (b)(3)) vs final "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice" throughout. Difference (triggering event).
- proposed (a)(3): "not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316" vs final "not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316". Difference.
- proposed (b)(3): "all other employees in the occupying a career position" typo vs final "all other employees occupying a career position." Typo/grammar; maybe skip.

§351.503:
- (a)(1): proposed "conjunction with the patterns of summary level in Sec. 430.208(d) of this chapter" vs final "5 CFR 430.208(e)". Difference (cross-reference paragraph).
- (b)(2): proposed "in accordance with Sec. 351.501 (as augmented...)" vs final "in accordance with Sec. 351.501 (as augmented...)" — final corrected by 2026-17335 to "paragraph (a) of this section (as augmented". Wait original final (line 5297) said "in accordance with Sec. 351.501 (as augmented by veterans'..." Hmm, final as published said "in accordance with Sec. 351.501 (as augmented by veterans' preference in accordance with Sec. 351.504)." The correction 2026-17335 changed it to "in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section (as augmented..." So final as corrected differs from proposed: proposed "in accordance with Sec. 351.501"; final corrected "in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section". Difference (cross-reference target: section vs paragraph). Q11 says "a change in which section, subpart or part a cross-reference points to is not citation format." Here proposed points to Sec. 351.501, final to paragraph (a) of this section (i.e., 351.503(a)). This is a change in which section/paragraph the cross-reference points to => counts. Hmm, but is it simply correction? It's a real difference.
- (c)(3): same.
- (c)(4): proposed "agency's' appropriate issuance(s)" typo vs final "agency's appropriate issuance(s)" — typo.
- (d): proposed "as set forth in Sec. 430.208(d) of this chapter" vs final "as set forth in Sec. 430.208(e)"; proposed "(i.e., a pattern A 'pass/fail', or pattern D system)" vs final "(i.e., a pattern A 'pass/fail', or pattern D system authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521)" — final adds clause. And correction further changes citation. Difference in cross-reference (d/e) and added authority text.
- (e)(1): proposed Sec. 430.208(d) vs final 430.208(e). Difference.
- (e)(2): proposed "(i.e., a level '4' rating if ... pattern C or G ..., or a level '5' rating if ... pattern B, E, F, or H summary level appraisal system)." Final adds "as authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521". Difference (added text).
- (f): same except proposed "prior to the date of issuance" vs final "prior to the date of issuance" same. (f)(2) same. (f)(3) same.
- (d)(3)/(e)(3): same.

§351.504:
- (a)(1)-(3): proposed "These employees should be identified" vs final "These employees must be identified" — "should" vs "must". Real difference? It changes obligation. I'd list maybe as a difference (category/verb) but it's wording. Q11 says differences that are only punctuation, capitalization or citation format don't count. "Should" vs "must" is substantive. List.
- (b): proposed "following paragraph (b)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, except as limited by paragraph (b)(4) or (5) of this section:" vs final "following paragraphs (b)(1), (2), or (3) of this section, except as limited by paragraph (b)(4) or (b)(5)": punctuation/format. Skip. Rest same.

§351.505:
- (b)(2): proposed "covered by Sec. 351.503(b)" vs final "covered by Sec. 351.504(b)". This is a cross-reference change to a different section! Definitely counts. Great catch: proposed wrong reference to 351.503(b), final corrected to 351.504(b).
- (c)(2): proposed "under paragraphs (a) and (b)" vs final "under paragraph (a) and paragraph (b)" — format.
- Other same.

§351.506:
- (c)(1): proposed "their performance credit ... and their service computation dates" vs final "the employee's performance credit ... and the employee's service computation date" — wording, not substantive.
- (c)(2): proposed "under Sec. 351.701(b) and (c)" vs final as published same, corrected by 2026-17335 to "under Sec. 351.701(b)". This is a cross-reference change (removes (c)) — and final 351.701 indeed has (b) and (c) still (pay rates) but assignment rights only (b). Does Q11 count? The proposed and final as published are same; correction changed final. Q11 says "regulatory text in the final rule (the amendments themselves, not the preambles)". Does "final rule" include corrections? Probably yes—the final regulatory text as corrected. But the correction is a separate document. I could note it in Q1/Q11 maybe. The question asks compare proposed rule with final rule; I'd include differences in final as corrected, noting correction. Hmm.
- (d): proposed "has no right to review" vs final "has no right under this section to review ... This paragraph does not limit any right of access available under another statute or regulation." Difference (final adds sentence). Yes.
- (f): same.

§351.507:
- proposed (b): "retained under any of this paragraph (b)" vs final "under any of these provisions". Wording. Skip.
- Others same.

§351.601(c): same.

§351.602: same.

§351.604: proposed amends 351.604 (revising (b), removing (d)); final does NOT amend 351.604 (because OPM decided not to finalize). This is a difference: proposed regulatory text had a revised 351.604(b); final has no amendment. Q11 asks differences between proposed and final regulatory text. Should list: proposed would have revised §351.604(b) and removed (d); final does not amend §351.604 at all (see preamble lines 250-253, 2845-2862). This is a significant difference. But is it "regulatory text"? The final has no text. I'd list it as an omission.

§351.605:
- (a): proposed "may use this paragraph (a)" vs final "may use this provision" — wording. Skip.
- (b): proposed includes all notification content inline; final (c) separate notice paragraph with similar content; final (d) retention register not required. Structural differences. Also proposed (b) says "An agency must provide any released competing employee with notification content in accordance with Sec. 351.802(a)(1), (3), (5), and (6) and (b), along the employee's competitive area and a statement..." vs final (c) adds "written notice in accordance with Sec. 351.801", "must identify the competitive area being abolished", and "The notice is not required to include the information described in Sec. 351.802(a)(2) or (a)(4)." Differences. Also final (b) says "The agency may provide for the exceptions under Sec. 351.608(c)-(f) without providing notice under Sec. 351.608(a)(4)." Same as proposed. Final (d) new: retention register not required and must not apply assignment rights. Proposed (b) last sentence "An agency may not apply assignment rights pursuant to subpart G of this part when using this paragraph (b)." Final moves to (d) with stronger "must not". Difference.

§351.606:
- (a): proposed "Armed Forces restoration rights. When an agency applies Sec. 351.601, it shall give retention priorities over other competing employees to each competing employee entitled under Sec. 351.209(b) to retention for, as applicable, 6 months or 1 year after restoration." Final completely rewritten with (a)(1)-(6): references Sec. 351.605 too, detailed mandatory exception, reassignment, OPM placement, etc. Major difference.
- (c): same.
- Note proposed cited Sec. 351.209(b) (wrong part?) vs final 353.209(b). Difference in cross-reference too.

§351.607: same.

§351.608:
- (a)(2): proposed "Career Transition Assistance Plan established under part 330, subpart E" vs final "subpart F". Cross-reference change to a different subpart => counts. Good catch.
- (a)(3): same.
- (a)(4): same.
- (b)-(g): same except (c) proposed "Administrative leave under part 630, subpart N, of this chapter" vs final "under 5 CFR part 630, subpart N" — format.
- (d)(2): proposed "requirements part 630, subpart D, of this chapter" vs final "requirements 5 CFR part 630, subpart D" — format.
- (e)(1)(ii): proposed long clause vs final condensed "because the employee is covered by a Federal leave system under an authority other than 5 U.S.C. chapter 63, a retirement law not referenced in Sec. 351.606(b), or a health benefits law other than 5 U.S.C. chapter 89" — wording, maybe no substantive difference. Skip or minor.
- (f), (g): same.

§351.701:
- proposed lacks subsection heading "(a) General." final adds heading. Not substantive.
- (a): proposed "minimally successful (Level 2)" vs final "minimally satisfactory (Level 2)". Difference in term? Level 2 description: 5 CFR 430.208(e) uses "Minimally Satisfactory". Proposed says "minimally successful" — likely typo. Is this "real"? Maybe list as term difference. Also final adds "(a) General." and "paragraph (b) of this section" etc. Citation format.
- (b)(2): proposed ends "(The agency uses ... assignment right.); and" vs final punctuation. Skip.
- (b)(3): proposed "pursuant the criteria set forth in Sec.Sec. 351.702 and 351.703" vs final "pursuant to the criteria set forth in Sec. 351.702 and Sec. 351.703." Format.
- (c)-(g): same.
- Note proposed 351.701(d) was eliminated? Both proposed and final are revised whole section; proposed new (d) is grade progression; old (d) restriction gone in both. So not a proposed-final difference.

§351.702(a)(4):
- (iii): proposed "Does not solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination." vs final "Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment." Difference in wording but same meaning.
- (iv): proposed "or another assessment provided: (A) It demonstrates..." vs final "or another assessment provided (1) it demonstrates..." — structural; correction fixes list structure. Probably format.
- (v): final adds new paragraph (v) exception for same position within 5 years. This is a major addition! Proposed had no (v). Yes, final adds (a)(4)(v). Difference.
- (a)(4) intro same.

§351.705(a): same.

§351.802:
- (a) intro: final adds "Except as otherwise provided in this part, a specific written notice under Sec. 351.801 must include:"; proposed had no intro (amended only (a)(2) and (3)). Difference: final adds introductory text. Yes.
- (a)(2): proposed "veteran status, tenure group and subgroup, service date, and three most recent ratings..." vs final "veterans' preference subgroup, tenure group and subgroup, service date, and three most recent ratings..." Difference (veteran status -> veterans' preference subgroup). Yes.
- (a)(3): proposed "A link to part 351 of this chapter and access..." vs final "A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency's records pertinent..." Difference in wording (access vs information on how to access). Is substantive? Maybe.
- There may be (a)(1) etc unchanged.

§351.805(b): final amends; proposed did not amend 351.805 at all (not in proposed TOC). This is a new amendment in final. Difference: final revises 351.805(b) to add amended notice rule; proposed had no such amendment. Yes (though Q11 asks differences between regulatory texts; this is an addition in final not in proposed).

§351.201/204 etc.

Also final added §351.203 "Restoration protected employee"; final added 351.202(d)(4); final added 351.402(c); final added 351.606(a) rewrite; final added 351.702(a)(4)(v); final added 351.802(a) intro; final added 351.805(b). Proposed had 351.604 amendment not finalized. Proposed 351.605 structure vs final.

Q11 asks "List every real difference between the two that you can find. For each, name the paragraph and say what the proposed text said and what the final text says. Do not stop at the changes that the final rule's own summary of its changes from the proposal mentions." So we should list all: including those mentioned in summary (e.g., USERRA 351.606, merit principles 351.204, competitive area safeguards 351.402(c), 351.202(d) notice, 351.605 wording, 351.805(b), 362.306 — but part 351 only), and unmentioned ones (351.502 issues vs receives; 351.202(d) removal of "term"/subpart C; 351.505(b)(2) cross-reference; 351.608(a)(2) subpart E -> F; 351.503(d)/(e) Sec. 430.208(d)->(e); 351.203 furlough phrase; 351.203 new restoration protected employee; 351.506(d) added sentence; 351.802(a)(2) veteran status -> veterans' preference subgroup; 351.604 not finalized; 351.701 "minimally successful" vs "minimally satisfactory"; 351.504 "should" vs "must"; 351.702(a)(4)(iii) wording; maybe 351.703? Not amended.)

Wait: Q11 says "Differences that are only punctuation, capitalization or citation format do not count; a change in which section, subpart or part a cross-reference points to is not citation format." This signals there are cross-reference changes to catch: 351.505(b)(2) Sec. 351.503(b) -> 351.504(b); 351.608(a)(2) subpart E -> F; 351.503(d)/(e) 430.208(d) -> (e); 351.203 rating of record 430.208(d) -> (e); 351.606(a) Sec. 351.209(b) -> Sec. 353.209(b); 351.503(b)(2) Sec. 351.501 -> paragraph (a) of this section (maybe). Also proposed 351.506(c)(2) Sec. 351.701(b) and (c) -> final published same, correction (b) only; but that's a correction difference, maybe not proposed-final.

Also perhaps final added "of this chapter" etc; ignore.

Now I need to read the final rule's preamble around section III to capture any statement about these changes, but Q11 explicitly says not to stop at summary of changes. We'll produce a comprehensive list from direct comparison.

    43  AGENCY: Merit Systems Protection Board.
    44  
    45  ACTION: Final rule.
    46  
    47  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    48  
    49  SUMMARY: The Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB or Board) is amending 
    50  its regulations to remove references to MSPB's jurisdiction over 
    51  probationary termination, suitability, and reduction-in-force (RIF) 
    52  appeals. This revision reflects the Office of Personnel Management's 
    53  (OPM's) rescission of the MSPB's jurisdiction to hear these types of 
    54  appeals. The rule retains MSPB's statutory jurisdiction over Foreign 
    55  Service reduction-in-force appeals under 22 U.S.C. 4010a.
    56  
    57  DATES: This final rule is effective on September 2, 2026. However, 
    58  consistent with OPM's rulemakings, the MSPB will not apply this rule to 
    59  pending cases or to newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken 
    60  before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings, and will continue to 
    61  adjudicate such probationary termination appeals, suitability appeals, 
    62  and RIF appeals.
    63  
    64  FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Gina K. Grippando, Clerk of the Board, 
    65  Merit Systems Protection Board, 1615 M Street NW, Washington, DC 20419; 
    66  phone: (202) 653-7200; fax: (202) 653-7130; or email: [email protected].
    67  
    68  SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
    69  
    70  I. Background
    71  
    72      The Civil Service Reform Act grants MSPB jurisdiction to hear 
    73  appeals of any action made appealable to MSPB under law, rule, or 
    74  regulation. 5 U.S.C. 7701(a). For the ease of MSPB's stakeholders, 
    75  MSPB's regulation at 5 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 1201.3 
    76  contains a list of the types of appeals MSPB has been granted 
    77  jurisdiction to hear. The current list includes 1201.3(a)(3), which 
    78  reflects appeal rights for employees who are terminated during their 
    79  initial or supervisory probationary period; 1201.3(a)(6), which 
    80  reflects appeals rights for employees subjected to a reduction-in-
    81  force; and 1201.3(a)(9), which reflects appeal rights for employees 
    82  subjected to a suitability action. OPM regulations previously granted 
    83  MSPB jurisdiction over each of these types of appeals, except for 
    84  reduction-in-force actions affecting a career or career candidate 
    85  appointee in the Foreign Service, over which MSPB exercises 
    86  jurisdiction pursuant to statute.
    87  
    88  A. Appeals for Terminations During Probationary or Trial Periods
    89  
    90      On June 24, 2025, OPM issued a final rule which stated that 
    91  Executive Order (E.O.) 14284, ``Strengthening Probationary Periods in 
    92  the Federal Service'' (90 FR 17729), issued on April 24, 2025, `` 
    93  `supersede[d] subpart H' [of part 315 of CFR title 5] and `rendered 
    94  [it] inoperative and without effect.' '' Accordingly, OPM's final rule 
    95  rescinded subpart H of CFR part 315, including 5 CFR 315.806, which 
    96  provided appeal rights to MSPB for employees serving an initial 
    97  appointment to a competitive service position who are terminated during 
    98  their probationary or trial period.
    99      Subsequently, effective September 2, 2026, OPM issued a final rule 
   100  revising 5 CFR 315.908(b) [of subpart I of part 315 CFR title 5] which 
   101  previously granted MSPB appeal rights to competitive service, 
   102  managerial or supervisory employees who alleged that an action under 
   103  that subpart, such as return to a nonsupervisory or nonmanagerial 
   104  position for failure to complete the probationary period, was based on 
   105  partisan political affiliation or marital status. The revised rule 
   106  rescinds MSPB appeal rights for these employees and instead provides a 
   107  right to appeal such actions to OPM.
   108      Consequently, MSPB now amends 5 CFR 1201.3(a)(3) to reflect the 
   109  rescission of these MSPB appeal rights. MSPB notes that OPM has 
   110  provided in its final rule that the rule covers actions effected from 
   111  September 2, 2026, forward, and therefore does not apply to any pending 
   112  MSPB appeals or future MSPB appeals filed based on actions effected 
   113  before September 2, 2026.
   114  
   115  B. Reduction in Force Appeals
   116  
   117      Effective September 2, 2026, OPM issued a final rule revising 5 CFR 
   118  351.901, which previously granted MSPB appeal rights to federal 
   119  employees subjected to a reduction-in-force. The new rule, in relevant 
   120  part, rescinds these MSPB appeal rights and instead provides reduction-
   121  in-force appeal rights exclusively to OPM. Consequently, MSPB now 
   122  amends 5 CFR 1201.3(a)(6) to reflect OPM's rescission of these 
   123  previously codified MSPB appeal rights. This amendment does not affect 
   124  the separate statutory right of a career or career candidate appointee 
   125  in the Foreign Service to appeal a RIF action to MSPB under 22 U.S.C. 
   126  4010a. The final rule retains that appeal right in redesignated 
   127  paragraph (a)(5) of 5 CFR 1201.3 but changes the referenced citation 
   128  from 22 U.S.C. 4011 to 22 U.S.C. 4010a, where the precise statutory 
   129  appeal reference is found.
   130      MSPB notes that OPM's final rule on RIF appeals applies only to a 
   131  RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF 
   132  notice on or after the effective date of the RIF appeals rule, and that 
   133  MSPB appeals of RIF actions taken before the effective date of OPM's 
   134  final rule may continue to be adjudicated through the MSPB process. 
   135  MSPB will therefore continue to adjudicate RIF appeals that are not 
   136  covered by OPM's final RIF appeals rule (i.e., because the RIF actions 
   137  were taken before the rule's effective date), and will accept such 
   138  cases for filing where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the 
   139  rule's effective date, and will not dismiss such appeals on the ground 
   140  that OPM's final rule displaced the MSPB's jurisdiction.
   141  
   142  C. Suitability Appeals
   143  
   144      Effective September 2, 2026, OPM issued a final rule revising 5 CFR 
   145  731.501, which previously granted MSPB appeal rights to individuals 
   146  subjected to a suitability action, which includes the cancellation of 
   147  eligibility, removal, cancellation of reinstatement eligibility, and 
   148  debarment. The new rule, in relevant part, rescinds these MSPB appeal 
   149  rights and provides suitability action appeal rights exclusively to 
   150  OPM. MSPB now amends 5 CFR 1201.3(a)(9) to reflect OPM's
   151  
   152  [[Page 51998]]
   153  
   154  rescission of these previously codified MSPB appeal rights.
   155      MSPB notes that OPM's suitability appeals rule does not apply to 
   156  suitability appeals filed with the MSPB before the effective date of 
   157  OPM's final rule, and that the MSPB may continue to adjudicate such 
   158  suitability appeals. MSPB will therefore continue to adjudicate such 
   159  suitability appeals that are not covered by OPM's final suitability 
   160  appeals rule, and will not dismiss such appeals on the ground that 
   161  OPM's final rule displaced the MSPB's jurisdiction.
   162  
   163  II. Summary of Changes
   164  
   165  Section 1201.3 Appellate Jurisdiction
   166  
   167      This amendment amends the list of appealable actions in section 
   168  1201.3(a) to remove references to appeal rights for employees in the 
   169  competitive service or in a managerial or supervisory position who are 
   170  terminated during their probationary or trial period; federal employees 
   171  subjected to a reduction in force; and federal applicants, appointees, 
   172  and employees subjected to a suitability action which includes the 
   173  cancellation of eligibility, removal, cancellation of reinstatement 
   174  eligibility, and debarment.
   175  
   176  III. Effective Date of Amendment
   177  
   178      The amendment described above will go into effect on September 2, 
   179  2026. However, as described above, and consistent with OPM's 
   180  rulemakings, the MSPB will not apply this amendment to probationary 
   181  termination, RIF, or suitability appeals pending as of September 2, 
   182  2026. Additionally, MSPB will adjudicate any RIF appeals it receives 
   183  after September 2, 2026, in which the RIF effective date preceded 
   184  September 2, 2026; and any probationary termination appeals pursuant to 
   185  5 CFR 315.908(b) it receives after September 2, 2026, in which the 
   186  probationary termination action was effected prior to September 2, 
   187  2026.
   188  
   189  IV. Regulatory Compliance
   190  
   191  A. Administrative Procedure Act
   192  
   193      Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), MSPB finds that there is good cause 
   194  to issue this final rule without prior notice and comment. This final 
   195  rule merely reflects the recission of the regulatory bases for MSPB's 
   196  jurisdiction. MSPB lacks any discretion regarding this change, and thus 
   197  lacks discretion in this rulemaking action. Accordingly, notice and 
   198  public comment procedures are unnecessary.
   199      Similarly, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3), MSPB finds that there is 
   200  good cause to make this final rule effective immediately upon 
   201  publication. This final rule merely reflects the recission of the 
   202  regulatory bases for MSPB's jurisdiction.
   203  
   204  B. Regulatory Impact Analysis: Executive Order 12866
   205  
   206      The MSPB has examined the impact of this rulemaking as required by 
   207  Executive Orders 12866 (Sept. 30, 1993) and 13563 (Jan. 18, 2011), 
   208  which direct agencies to evaluate the benefits and costs of the action. 
   209  A regulatory impact analysis must be prepared for rules with effects of 
   210  $100 million or more in any one year. This rulemaking does not reach 
   211  that threshold but has otherwise been designated as a ``significant 
   212  regulatory action'' under section 3(f) of Executive Order 12866, as 
   213  supplemented by Executive Order 13563.
   214  
   215  C. Regulatory Flexibility Act
   216  
   217      The MSPB certifies that this rulemaking will not have a significant 
   218  economic impact on a substantial number of small entities because OPM's 
   219  rule will apply only to Federal agencies, employees, or applicants for 
   220  employment, and the MSPB's rule does not in itself effect any change, 
   221  but only reflects OPM's amendments to MSPB's jurisdiction.
   222  
   223  D. Paperwork Reduction Act
   224  
   225      This document does not contain information collection requirements 
   226  subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, Public Law 104-13 (44 
   227  U.S.C. Chapter 35).
   228  
   229  E. Executive Order 13132, Federalism
   230  
   231      This regulation will not have substantial direct effect on the 
   232  States, on the relationship between the National Government and the 
   233  States, or on distribution of power and responsibilities among the 
   234  various levels of government. Therefore, in accordance with Executive 
   235  Order 13132 (Aug. 10, 1999), it is determined that this rule does not

   239  F. Executive Order 12988, Civil Justice Reform
   240  
   241      This regulation meets the applicable standards set forth in section

   246      This rulemaking will not result in the expenditure by State, local,

content.text:
Key MSPB details:
- DATES (lines 57-62): effective Sept 2, 2026; but will not apply to pending cases or newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings; continue to adjudicate such RIF appeals.
- Section III (lines 176-187): "MSPB will adjudicate any RIF appeals it receives after September 2, 2026, in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026." — Note inconsistency within MSPB rule: earlier it says "agency actions taken before the effective date" and "where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date" (lines 130-140) vs Section III says "RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026". This is Q14(iii): inconsistency within the Board's rule about which RIF appeals the Board will still hear: notice issued before vs action taken/effective date before. Also compare with OPM rule: applies only to RIF actions for which specific notice issued on/after Sept 2, 2026 (DATES lines 83-86), so OPM rule's trigger is notice issuance; MSPB's Section III uses RIF effective date; MSPB's Background uses "actions taken before the effective date" and "notice issued before". So multiple inconsistencies:
  * DATES: "agency actions taken before the effective date" (action taken)
  * Background B: "RIF actions were taken before the rule's effective date" and "where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date" (notice issued)
  * Section III: "RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026" (RIF effective date)
  These are three different triggers. Q14(iii) wants inconsistencies within Board's rule or between Board's rule and OPM's rule about which RIF appeals Board will still hear. Great.

Also note line 130-134 says "OPM's final rule on RIF appeals applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice on or after the effective date..." consistent with OPM.

Now read OPM appeals final rule: TOC summary of changes (lines 108-344), then regulatory text 4212-4700. Let me read 72-344 first.
